findings.title: Garden refuge as guest reception
findings.claim: The believer and the defiantly disobedient person are declared unequal in 32:18, and 32:19–20 gives that distinction opposed destinations. In the focus, belief and sound action lead to a garden refuge that is also described as prepared provision for a guest; the next ayah applies mawa to the Fire and depicts attempted departure followed by compulsory return. The positive destination is a sheltered welcome, while the same destination term can stand in the opposing half without making that half hospitable.
findings.mechanism: The focus word mawa carries the gathering and sheltering place sense, while nuzul supplies an independent guest-provision image. The next ayah reuses mawa for the Fire; its exit and return sequence tests that opposite destination as inescapable. The contact makes the value of each destination emerge through its contents and the way its occupants are received. The preceding believer–fasiq contrast and the focus's pairing of belief with sound acts keep the promised welcome attached to the group and its deeds.
findings.reader_payoff: The outcome becomes a concrete scene of reception: one group arrives at a tree-covered refuge with a prepared guest's portion, while the neighboring passage makes the opposing enclosure's forced return visible.
findings.containment: The focus's refuge sense remains present; the inference is that gardens and hospitality supply its welcome in this contrast. The packet does not establish that mawa is intrinsically neutral, nor does it disclose the hidden reward's full contents. The distinction remains tied to the explicit belief, action, and destination clauses.

epistemic.reason: The garden and hospitality nomination is trusted and the focus branches are registered. The represented HFT adds exact in-pericope Arabic and matching coordinates, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound, so the exit and return roles remain attributed.

findings.title: Work as a continuing trajectory
findings.claim: The focus's two work forms sit within a pericope that presents work as an action with a history and a lived consequence. The speakers at 32:12 ask to return so they can do righteous work; 32:14 connects tasting punishment to what people did; 32:17 describes hidden recompense according to work; and 32:19 gives the garden as the hospitable outcome of what the believers used to do. This leaves both a sustained pattern and a more itemized account in view.
findings.mechanism: The focus first names completed work and then uses a habitual clause with the same root. Context supplies a denied request to return and act, negative tasting tied to work, and positive recompense tied to work. These links make the closing work clause read as a history that returns in an experienced outcome, with guest provision giving that outcome concrete form.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause can be heard as the destination of sustained purposeful practice, while the explicit recompense formulas still allow a reading in terms of deeds and their corresponding account.
findings.containment: The HFT author explicitly keeps a live alternative in which the passage describes a strictly itemized legal account. The packet does not settle between that account and a durable trajectory, and this finding adds the latter without removing the former.

epistemic.reason: Every cited HFT anchor has supplied Arabic and complete in-pericope coverage. The root, word indices, and causal synthesis are from a legacy_unbound reader trace, so they are retained as attributed contextual evidence.

findings.title: Devotion answered with lodging
findings.claim: The pericope places embodied worship and the leaving of ordinary beds immediately before a promise of refuge and guest provision. The lodging can therefore be read as answering a pattern of bodily devotion that repeatedly gave up ordinary rest, while the earlier acts may also simply exemplify the sound deeds named in the focus.
findings.mechanism: The HFT traces name falling and prostration in 32:15, then separation from beds in 32:16. The focus shifts from those bodily acts to mawa, a sheltering place, and nuzul, provision prepared for a guest. That contact makes the garden reception feel like an answer to relinquished rest rather than a description of effortless rest alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The promised rest has a lived prehistory: bodies that lowered themselves and left their beds are pictured later as received and lodged.
findings.containment: The exact relation is a legacy_unbound contextual inference. The packet leaves live the alternative that the earlier practices are examples of righteous deeds rather than a direct exchange of rest for lodging; no equivalence of effort and reward is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The three exact Arabic anchors are supplied and the HFT coordinates match their surfaces. Word segmentation, roots, and the embodied-rest relation remain attributed to a legacy_unbound source.

findings.title: The garden names the hidden reward
findings.claim: The focus names gardens immediately after 32:17 describes a hidden reward for them. This activates both the covering image of the j-n-n family and the branch that treats jannat as the afterlife reward dwelling with benefits presently hidden; the contextual fit leaves the ordinary garden image available.
findings.mechanism: The focus garden is the carrier, and 32:17's explicit hidden-reward wording is the independent trigger. Their contact lets the next ayah give a name and destination to what the preceding ayah says had been hidden, while the garden's covering image remains part of the same word family.
findings.reader_payoff: The garden is perceived both as a concrete garden and as the named form of an unseen promised reward.
findings.containment: The packet does not decide the word's naming history between the earthly tree-covered garden and hidden afterlife benefits, nor does it disclose the hidden reward's contents. This is a contextual activation, not a claim that the physical garden sense disappears.

epistemic.reason: The preceding ayah's exact Arabic and its relation to the focus are supplied through a legacy_unbound HFT projection. The focus branch records are present, and the claim is limited to the textual contact.
